page_title: Pake · Turn any website into a lightweight desktop app

sources.entry: Pake - Turn any website into a lightweight desktop app with its own icon, window and Dock entry.

summary.name: Pake
summary.one_liner: Pake turns any website into a lightweight desktop app for Mac, Windows and Linux, either through a no-compiler desktop app or the free, open-source Pake CLI.
use_cases: Turn a web service like YouTube Music into a standalone desktop app
Package an internal or personal website as a Dock app on Mac
Build a Windows or Linux installer from a URL
Create small desktop wrappers without writing an app
Automate app builds from the terminal or GitHub Actions
summary.what_it_does: Pake takes a website URL and produces a native installer: a .dmg on Mac, an .msi on Windows, or a .deb, AppImage or .rpm on Linux. Each app gets its own icon, window and Dock entry. A desktop app version requires no compiler, and the free Pake CLI can be installed via npm and run with a single command. Pake renders pages with the browser already installed on the computer, which keeps apps usually under 10 MB, unlike bundled-browser frameworks such as Electron. The first build sets up Rust, and later builds are faster; builds can also run online through GitHub Actions.
notable: Uses the system's installed browser engine, so apps are usually under 10 MB
Pay-once license at $15 for unlimited apps on up to 3 computers
Gallery of ready-made desktop apps built from each release
caveats: Some sites may render slightly differently across operating systems because it uses the system browser
Building more than 2 apps requires the $15 one-time license
The first build requires installing Rust
